source_title: Junie Release 1362.47 (first of a series of model-support releases)
claim_summary: Release-channel notes add third-party models throughout the window: Opus 4.7 (Apr 16), GPT 5.5 (Apr 27), Grok 4.3 (May 18), Gemini 3.5 Flash (May 20), Opus 4.8 (May 28), Claude Fable 5 (Jun 10), GPT-5.6 (Jul 9), Grok 4.5 (Jul 17), Gemini 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash Lite (Jul 21), Claude Opus 5 (Jul 24), Grok 4.6 (Aug 12), Gemini 3.7 Flash (Aug 13), Claude Fable 5.1 (Sep 1), Gemini 3.8 Flash (Sep 2), GPT-6 Astra (Sep 4), Grok 4.7/Claude Opus 5.5/GPT-6 Sol and Luna (Sep 22), Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT 6.1 Sol (Sep 29), Claude Haiku 5.5 (Oct 12)
feature: multi-vendor model support in the coding agent
limitation: Model availability per plan/region not checked; GitHub API lists 61 Release-channel and about 1,770 Nightly releases in window, so release count is not a feature count; repository licence is proprietary (LICENSE.md: all rights reserved, JetBrains AI Service terms)

claim_summary: Bulletin (publication 2026-04-17, severity Medium): command execution was possible via a malicious project file; resolved in Junie 252.549.29; credited to a Mindgard researcher
feature: agent handling of untrusted project files
limitation: Severity conflict: JetBrains CNA CVSS 3.1 = 5.8 (AV:L/AC:H/UI:R) vs NVD primary = 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/UI:N) in the NVD record; exploitation in the wild unknown; bulletin page is client-rendered, data read from its JSON feed resources.jetbrains.com/storage/issues-fixed/data.json

source_title: SWE-rebench Leaderboard (news entry 2026-04-19 and default view)
claim_summary: Leaderboard news: 'Re-run the Junie with Claude Opus 4.6 as the primary model' (Apr 19). Default view at access (time window 15/05/2026-01/07/2026, 111 problems from 65 repositories): Junie (Agent) 61.8% +/- 0.54% resolved, 73.9% pass@5, $0.81 per problem, ranked 6th overall behind five raw models (Fable 5, Grok 4.5, Opus 5, GLM-5.2, GPT-5.6 Sol) and first among agent rows, ahead of Claude Code at 60.4% +/- 1.03% resolved but with lower pass@5 (73.9% vs 75.7%) and lower cost per problem ($0.81 vs $3.39)
limitation: Mutable living page, values depend on the selected window; Junie was added as a 'reference evaluation' (Mar 9) whose setup may involve the vendor; vendor's Jun 17 quote (61.6% / 72.7%, first among agents) differs slightly from the default view; not reproduced here

claim_summary: Plan Mode 2.0: a live design document capturing scope, key decisions and reasoning before any code is written, kept updated as requirements evolve
limitation: No independent evidence that plans reduce review or rework

claim_summary: Model effort control per model via /effort or --effort; GPT 5.5 supported
limitation: Effect of effort settings on accepted-task cost not measured

claim_summary: Annual highlights (covering 2025) state that JetBrains AI tools reached a six-figure active paid user count in Q4 2025, with the largest quarter-over-quarter gain (+101.33%) in Q2 2025; AI-MAU counts paying users only; describes Mellum as 'JetBrains' proprietary LLM' for code completion and ACP as developed by JetBrains and Zed
limitation: Page carries no visible date; published_utc taken from the team-blog announcement URL path (blog.jetbrains.com/team/2026/04/27/...) listed in the blog sitemap; paid-user counts are not task value; 'proprietary' wording conflicts with the Apache-2.0 Mellum weights on Hugging Face

claim_summary: Local Code Review (/review): review your changes before committing; later releases add an Apply suggestion UI (Sep 14) and immediate start when a commit, branch, range or PR is named (Oct 6)
limitation: Review quality, false-positive rate and reviewer time not measured

claim_summary: Debug Agent: Junie can connect to the IDE (version 2026.1.1 or later required) and set breakpoints to debug the app; release names switch to calendar-style versions (26.5.11)
limitation: IDE-coupled capability; not independently exercised

claim_summary: Remote Access (/remote) to a Junie session from a browser on any device; skill mentioning ($skill-name, /skills); /plan and /debug mode switching; Grok 4.3 supported
limitation: Authentication and exposure model of remote access not reviewed

source_title: No More JetBrains Products for Me
claim_summary: A paying CLion user reports switching to Zed, citing slow startup, project switching, re-indexing, Remote Development disconnects and large install size
limitation: Single user's experience on older hardware; page carries no date, so published_utc is the Hacker News submission date (2026-05-18, 154 points); not a measurement

claim_summary: First stable release of the Kotlin agent framework: stable/beta module split so production code can pin APIs, removal of all deprecated APIs, redesigned Java interop, HTTP transport decoupled from Ktor, OpenTelemetry on Kotlin Multiplatform, Anthropic prompt caching; preceded by three previews (May 17-20)
limitation: Downstream adoption not measured; GitHub stars are not reuse evidence

claim_summary: Extensions (/extensions): ready-to-use bundles of skills, MCPs, commands, guidelines and agents, with connection to existing plugin marketplaces
limitation: Supply-chain review of third-party bundles not documented here; compare marketplace malware report (Jun 16 row)

source_title: Mellum2 Goes Open Source: A Fast Model for AI Workflows
claim_summary: JetBrains open-sources Mellum2 under Apache 2.0: a 12B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 2.5B active parameters per token, trained from scratch on natural language and code (not multimodal), positioned for routing, Q&A, sub-agents and private deployment; vendor says it is competitive with similar-sized models while cutting inference time to less than half
availability: weights on Hugging Face (Base, Instruct, Thinking, SFT variants and GGUF quantisations)
limitation: Benchmarks are vendor-run (technical report not read); the Base, Instruct, Thinking and SFT Hugging Face repos were created 2026-05-26 (a Mellum2-12B-A2.5B-Base-Pretrain repo reports createdAt 2026-04-07, before the window; GGUF repos 2026-06-03) and the model cards carry license: apache-2.0 and 64 experts / 8 active / 131,072-token context; the Apr 27 annual highlights still call Mellum 'proprietary'

claim_summary: Worktree support (/worktree): manage Git worktrees directly from the agent
feature: parallel work isolation via git worktrees
limitation: Isolation is a workflow convenience, not a security sandbox

claim_summary: Kotlin 2.4.0 released (RC May 13, RC2 May 27); followed by 2.4.10 (Jul 14), 2.4.20 (Sep 7), 2.4.21 (Oct 8) and 2.5.0-Beta1 (Sep 23)
limitation: Changelog lists issue IDs only; no AI-specific claim; included as baseline OSS cadence

claim_summary: First new release under the Kotlin Toolchain name, v0.11.0 (published 2026-06-04 20:52 UTC, with breaking changes and a link to a release blog post); the repository (created 2026-05-11, Apache-2.0) also re-published the historical Amper tags v0.1.0-v0.10.0 the same day; the JetBrains/amper README now says Amper is part of Kotlin Toolchain and the Amper repository is archived and no longer maintained
availability: v0.x releases (26 release objects in window, 20 of them re-published historical Amper tags)
limitation: Release blog post (blog.jetbrains.com/amper/2026/06/kotlin-toolchain-0-11/) not read; date of the Amper archival not available from the API; migration cost for Amper users not measured

source_title: Multiple JetBrains IDE plugins caught stealing AI keys
claim_summary: Security vendor reports at least 15 Marketplace plugins from seven vendor accounts posing as DeepSeek-based AI coding assistants that send the user's AI provider API key to a hard-coded server over plain HTTP; earliest versions Oct 2025, new ones still released in June 2026; notes JetBrains plugins pass a manual review that this logic slipped through
feature: IDE plugin supply chain; AI API keys
limitation: Commercially interested source (sells device protection); download counts may be inflated per the report; JetBrains response or removal not confirmed in this pass

source_title: Junie: The JetBrains AI Coding Agent Leaves Beta
claim_summary: Junie leaves Beta: plan mode with plans stored in .junie/plans, agentic use of the IDE debugger, remote control of async tasks, code review from GitHub Actions/GitLab or /review, IDE integration rebuilt on ACP, database access via DataGrip, BYOK and local runtimes (LiteLLM, LM Studio, Ollama); quotes a Nebius research lead that Junie placed first among agents on SWE-rebench with 61.6% resolved and 72.7% pass@5
feature: coding agent GA across IDE and CLI
availability: GA in JetBrains IDEs and Junie CLI; debugger features need an AI subscription
limitation: Benchmark figure is a vendor quotation; the post expands ACP as 'Agent Communication Protocol' while other JetBrains pages use 'Agent Client Protocol'; see SWE-rebench row for the current leaderboard values

claim_summary: Bulletin (Low): project settings disclosure via the MCP was possible; resolved in YouTrack 2026.2.16593

claim_summary: Auto Mode: Junie automatically approves commands; on-demand session compression (/compress); context-window indicator

claim_summary: Subagent support (vendor says for improved quality and cost efficiency) and a redesigned thoughts-centric UI

claim_summary: Apache-2.0 repository (created 2026-07-08) for a lightweight IDE/GUI around the third-party Pi coding agent; 103 releases in window up to v0.1.6 (Oct 6); the ThinkRail blog (2026-08-19) calls it backed by JetBrains, early stage, one git branch per session
feature: GUI for a third-party coding agent
limitation: Install instructions pipe a remote script to the shell; maturity and support unknown

source_title: Introducing JetBrains Context: Repository Intelligence for Coding Agents
claim_summary: Early access of a repository-intelligence layer (jbcontext CLI) for agents such as Claude Agent, OpenAI Codex and Junie: incremental semantic index, semantic retrieval and multi-repo search including repositories not checked out locally; vendor says that on 205 SWE-bench tasks, 175 production-monorepo tasks and 1,953 code-localisation tasks it reduced agent turns by up to 68%, latency by up to 59% and execution cost by up to 48%; included at no extra cost with a JetBrains AI licence; 'source code is not stored on JetBrains Context servers'
feature: semantic code retrieval for third-party agents
availability: early access; requires JetBrains AI licence
limitation: 'Up to' figures from vendor evaluation; no per-benchmark medians or task-acceptance rates given; install instructions use a GET-request installer; where the index is stored when repositories are not checked out locally is not explained; JetBrains/context GitHub repository has no licence field

source_title: Junie Can Now Run Entirely on Your Mac - No Credits, No Cloud
claim_summary: Junie Local runs the agent on-device via /local with Qwen3.6-27B at 4-bit (about 20 GB download), requires an M5 Mac with 64 GB RAM, is free with no registration or credits; vendor says the model scored on par with Sonnet 4.5 on JetBrains' private test set and GPT-5 medium slightly higher; prototypes for DGX Spark and RTX 5090
availability: free; M5 Mac with 64 GB RAM
limitation: Private benchmark; product page lists ~40 GB of disk for the model download alongside about 20 GB of model weights (a disk requirement, not a conflicting download size); also published at blog.jetbrains.com/junie/2026/08/junie-local-launch/

source_title: JetBrains Releases Junie Local, Bringing Its Coding Agent Fully On-Device to Macs
claim_summary: Trade publication relays the launch and notes the hardware cost: cheapest qualifying Mac it found was a $4,499 MacBook Pro configuration; JetBrains has not given a timeline for Linux, Windows or lower-memory Macs
limitation: Secondary report of the vendor announcement; it maps the private benchmark to public SWE-bench scores, which the vendor did not claim; one price search, not a market survey

claim_summary: JetBrains reports unauthorised access to Cadence, its hosted service (sunset announced Mar 31, shutdown scheduled Aug 31) that ran PyCharm projects on cloud compute via TeamCity; the environment was exploited through TeamCity CVE-2026-63077; IoCs cover activity from Aug 8 onwards; the Sep 3 update says the attacker could have reached storage with current users' email addresses, project source code and credentials, and users were told to rotate all secrets and treat executions as untrusted
feature: vendor-hosted execution of user code; patch lag on own infrastructure
limitation: Status 'corrected' because the post was revised on Aug 31, Sep 1 and Sep 3, widening the stated exposure; vendor's own account; number of affected users not stated; event_date_utc is the start of the IoC activity window, not a confirmed intrusion date; the bulletin for CVE-2026-63077 was published Jul 27

claim_summary: New skills module supporting the Agent Skills specification (discovery, catalog prompts) and a module to run Koog agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime; 1.3.0 (Sep 24) adds ready-made model definitions for current providers
feature: portable agent skills in an OSS framework
limitation: Interoperability with other skill consumers not tested

product: JetBrains Air (Air in IDEs, Air Teams, Air Governance)
source_title: JetBrains Air: Building a System of Products for Agentic Software Development
claim_summary: JetBrains brings its agentic work together as JetBrains Air: Air in JetBrains IDEs, Air Teams (new), Air Governance (formerly JetBrains Central: policy, audit, cost management); Junie to be supported across all Air surfaces; ACP Registry for third-party agents; states 'code becomes cheaper to generate but more expensive to verify' and that organisational economics of agents are 'much harder to prove'; future mobile/remote surfaces and event-triggered workflows announced without dates

source_title: Junie Lite: a free model for the work that never needed a frontier one
claim_summary: Free Junie tier for every JetBrains account in Air and Junie CLI, running Qwen 3.6 27B on JetBrains infrastructure with 'virtually unlimited' usage; prompts and code not shared with the model provider or used for training; added in CLI release 26.9.22 (3419.26) on Oct 1
limitation: Body says 'isn't a trial, and there's no countdown*' while the footnote says the offer is valid until 31 Dec 2026 and terms/models may change

source_title: Mellum2.1 Gets to Work: A Fast Open Model for Coding Agents
claim_summary: Mellum2.1 (same 12B MoE / 2.5B active architecture, Apache 2.0) retrained with reinforcement learning in real repository sandboxes for coding agents and sub-agents on own hardware; model card (self-reported by JetBrains) gives SWE-bench Verified 47.0 vs 2.0 for Mellum2 Thinking and 50.0 for Qwen3.5 (9B), Terminal-Bench 2.1 17.4 vs 21.7 for Qwen3.5 (9B)
limitation: All scores self-reported; the post (Oct 8) says GGUF builds are 'coming soon' while a Mellum2.1 GGUF repository on Hugging Face was created Oct 7 (order of publication unclear); a comparable-size open model scores higher on both agentic benchmarks in the vendor's own table
